# Nexus

> Nexus is a free, open-source (Apache-2.0), offline-first desktop app by Luka Stojiljković that combines tasks, calendar, notes, studying, finance, habits, fitness, files, tools and a canvas in one workspace, beside offline Wikipedia, signed content packs and local language models. Everything is stored in an encrypted database on the user's own computer, and everything the user writes works with the network off. It runs on Windows 10 and 11, Linux and macOS, and its interface is in Serbian and English.

Key facts:

- 43 modules in six groups, beside the dashboard and settings. Every module is visible on a new install, and a person may hide or reorder what they do not use. Plan: tasks, calendar, habits, focus and timers. Knowledge: notes, documents, study, an offline Wikipedia reader for Kiwix ZIM files, a reader, a translator, maps, astronomy, a recorder and a local assistant. Life: finance, fitness, an encrypted private vault, pantry, cookbook, car and an emergency card. Culture: a library, a culture guide and a gallery for art packs, images from downloaded references, and a person's own encrypted pictures. Make: an electronics workbench that generates Arduino sketches and ROS 2 packages, a canvas, CAD and 3D-print file viewers, a scanner, a calculator, signals, a lab, mini apps, tools and professional toolkits. Play: cards, chess, board games, puzzles and arcade games.
- Assistant: a local language model (llama.cpp, with GGUF models from Hugging Face) that acts in every module through 207 of the app's own tools, asks before each change, answers from the user's notes, packs, the app's manual and offline Wikipedia with its sources named, and docks beside any page.
- Translator and maps: translation between 202 languages by Meta's NLLB-200, run on the user's own computer from a signed model pack in one of three sizes; maps of any country, continent or the whole world, cut at a chosen detail from the Protomaps build of OpenStreetMap, with place search, pins and distance measurement.
- Study: exam countdowns, spaced-repetition flashcards, cloze and step-by-step cards, typeset maths, Anki deck import, and an exam planner that schedules study blocks and re-plans when the user falls behind.
- Storage: one SQLite database encrypted at rest. An account can use a passcode, a system key vault plus Recovery Kit, or explicit device-convenience mode when no key vault is available. Attachments are AES-256-GCM encrypted. Private notes always require their own credential and have their own Recovery Kit.
- Network: offline by default. On first start the user picks **Offline only** (no network call of any kind, enforced by a CI check), **Offline + update checks** (Nexus contacts GitHub only to check for and download a new version of itself) or **Downloads** (also the content packs, map regions, Kiwix libraries and Hugging Face models the user chooses, from a compiled-in list of hosts). Notes and data never leave the computer. It collects no data, has no online account and has no server: there is no cloud and no sync. Data moves to another computer as an exported archive, optionally password-protected.
- Data portability: a full export into one sealed archive that can be restored or merged, plus scheduled encrypted backups.
- Platforms: Windows 10 and 11 (per-user installer) and Linux (AppImage, tarball and a Gentoo ebuild) on x64, and macOS on Apple silicon (an unsigned dmg). Linux does not require a keyring; without a system vault Nexus uses an owner-only local guard. The Windows installer isn't code-signed yet.
- Built with Electron, React 19 and TypeScript in a pnpm and Turborepo monorepo.

- [Latest release](https://github.com/lukastojiljkovic/Nexus/releases/latest): Windows installer, Linux AppImage and macOS dmg
